edges.description: Temperature-induced virulence factors enable Y. pestis to replicate rapidly in the airways after lung seeding.
edges.source: Inhaled or Hematogenous Yersinia pestis Lung Seeding

edges.description: Pla-supported airway replication amplifies the bacterial population during the early anti-inflammatory phase of pneumonic plague.
Delayed early inflammation permits unchecked pulmonary bacterial growth before bacterial burden triggers an abrupt pro-inflammatory lung-injury phase.
Infection of the lung manifests clinically as pneumonia.
Fulminant pneumonia can produce bloody sputum and hemoptysis.
Exudative bronchopneumonia produces shortness of breath.
Pulmonary inflammation and airway exudate produce cough.
Fulminant lower-respiratory infection can cause chest pain.
The abrupt pro-inflammatory phase produces systemic fever.
Rapid pulmonary Y. pestis proliferation can progress to bacteremia and systemic septic complications.
Severe septicemic plague can trigger consumptive coagulopathy as a terminal complication.
Severe exudative bronchopneumonia can progress to respiratory failure.

nodes.description: The initially anti-inflammatory pulmonary infection rapidly flips to a highly pro-inflammatory phase with purulent multifocal exudative bronchopneumonia, alveolar injury, bloody sputum, and clinical pneumonia.

evidence.reference_title: Progression of primary pneumonic plague: a mouse model of infection, pathology, and bacterial transcriptional activity.
evidence.snippet: begins with an antiinflammatory state in the first 24-36 h that rapidly progresses to a highly proinflammatory state by 48 h

evidence.reference_title: Yersinia pestis and plague: an updated view on evolution, virulence determinants, immune subversion, vaccination, and diagnostics.
evidence.snippet: Some of these immunogenic proteins as well as the capsular antigen F1 are exploited for diagnostic purposes, which are critical in the context of the rapid onset of death in the absence of antibiotic treatment (less than a week for bubonic plague and <48 h for pneumonic plague).

nodes.description: During the first 24 to 36 hours in the lung, Y. pestis combines Yop delivery, LcrV-induced IL-10 signaling, and F1 capsule-mediated antiphagocytosis to delay leukocyte recruitment and suppress innate inflammatory control.

evidence.reference_title: The Yersinia pestis type III secretion system: expression, assembly and role in the evasion of host defenses.
evidence.snippet: Yersinia pestis, the etiologic agent of plague, utilizes a type III secretion system (T3SS) to subvert the defenses of its mammalian hosts.

evidence.reference_title: Type 3 secretion system induced leukotriene B4 synthesis by leukocytes is actively inhibited by Yersinia pestis to evade early immune recognition.
evidence.snippet: several Yop effectors secreted through the T3SS effectively inhibit this host response

evidence.reference_title: Yersinia V-antigen exploits toll-like receptor 2 and CD14 for interleukin 10-mediated immunosuppression.
evidence.snippet: LcrV signals in a CD14- and toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2)-dependent fashion leading to immunosuppression by interleukin 10 induction

evidence.reference_title: Role of fraction 1 antigen of Yersinia pestis in inhibition of phagocytosis.
evidence.snippet: F1 and the virulence plasmid-encoded type III system act in concert to make Y. pestis highly resistant to uptake by phagocytes.

nodes.description: Y. pestis reaches the lung either directly through inhaled infectious respiratory droplets or secondarily through hematogenous spread from another infected focus, establishing pulmonary infection rather than the draining-lymph-node or primary bloodstream forms of plague.
nodes.id: Inhaled or Hematogenous Yersinia pestis Lung Seeding

nodes.description: The Y. pestis plasminogen activator Pla is required for primary pneumonic plague and permits rapid airway replication rather than inflammatory clearance and lung repair.

evidence.reference_title: A plasminogen-activating protease specifically controls the development of primary pneumonic plague.
evidence.snippet: Pla allows Y. pestis to replicate rapidly in the airways, causing a lethal fulminant pneumonia

evidence.reference_title: Yersinia pestis and plague: an updated view on evolution, virulence determinants, immune subversion, vaccination, and diagnostics.
evidence.snippet: unrestricted bacterial replication in lymph nodes (bubonic plague) and in lungs (pneumonic plague)
